questions.text: What is the main purpose of a Spec in Kiro?

options.label: Define requirements, design, and implementation tasks in a structured way
Store team conventions and standards, loading them automatically in every interaction
Package documentation and MCP servers to expand Kiro's capabilities in a modular way
Connect Kiro to external tools and services through a standardized protocol

questions.explanation: A Spec is a set of structured artifacts that records requirements or bug analysis, design, and tasks. These artifacts keep the reasoning and implementation plan reviewable.

questions.text: Every Spec generates three main files: requirements.md or bugfix.md in the first phase, followed by design.md and tasks.md.
questions.explanation: True. Feature Specs use `requirements.md`; Bugfix Specs use `bugfix.md`. Both complete the set with `design.md` and `tasks.md`.

questions.text: A new authentication feature involves product, security, and frontend stakeholders; its criteria still need alignment before architecture. Which flow is most appropriate?

options.label: Requirements-First Feature Spec: align user stories and criteria, then generate design and tasks
Design-First Feature Spec: freeze the architecture first and derive requirements without stakeholder review
Bugfix Spec: treat the missing feature as defective behavior and preserve everything else as unchanged behavior

questions.explanation: Because this is a new feature whose criteria still need alignment, Requirements-First consolidates requirements before design. Design-First is also a Feature Spec flow, but it is better suited when the technical architecture is already clear and should drive requirements.

questions.text: After selecting the Requirements-First workflow, arrange the steps below, including the optional analysis before design:

options.label: Generate requirements.md with user stories and acceptance criteria
Optionally analyze and refine the requirements to eliminate ambiguities
Generate design.md with architecture and components
Generate tasks.md with discrete and trackable tasks
Implement the feature by executing the tasks

questions.explanation: In the Requirements-First workflow, Kiro first generates requirements.md. After reviewing the requirements, you can use Analyze Requirements to find ambiguities, inconsistencies, and gaps before proceeding to design, but this analysis is optional. Kiro then generates design.md and tasks.md, and the tasks are executed to implement the feature.
